newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oil output normal at N. Sea Statfjord, Gullfaks.
newsitem.headline: Oil output normal at N. Sea Statfjord, Gullfaks.

text.p: Offshore crude loadings and production was back to normal on Tuesday at the North Sea Statfjord and Gullfaks developments, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said.
"Tankers are loading, everything is okay. We are at full production," a spokeswoman for Statoil said.
Shuttle tankers were able to hook up to the offshore loading buoys late on Monday, the first time there has been a break in stormy weather since Friday.
Production was cut to a bare minimum due to brimming storage tanks. Statoil said output was brought back to normal as tankers loaded.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) and processes oil from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre development, which add roughly 370,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 115,000 bpd from the Tordis and Vigdis fields.
Bjoern Schibevaag, spokesman for Saga Petroleum ASA, said Snorre began pumping at 2040 GMT on Monday, while Vigdis resumed output at 0445 GMT on Tuesday.
"We should reached between 30 and 40,000 bpd at Vigdis but they are still testing equipment," he said. Vigdis came onstream in January.
"Tordis goes with Gullfaks C. If that's in production then so is Tordis," Schibevaag said.
